legend: Flow cytometry dot plots show the immunophenotype of blasts (red), immature monocytes (cyan), mature monocytes (purple), lymphocytes (light blue), and granulocytes (brown). The blasts show dim to moderate CD45 and low side scatter on a log scale (A), bright CD11c and moderate CD123 (B), variable CD34 and moderate CD64 (C), variable CD15 and partial (subset) CD7 (D), negative CD14 (E), bright CD33 and HLA-DR (F), moderate CD36 and variable CD117 (G), and dim CD4 (H) expression.
Bone marrow biopsy shows sheets of blasts, varying in size from intermediate to large, with fine chromatin, distinct nucleoli, and irregular lobular nuclear contours.

Bone marrow aspirate shows a blast morphology with intermediate to large cells, with modest amounts of pale basophilic cytoplasm and oval to somewhat reniform nuclear contours with fine chromatin (Giemsa) (<<30686>>). At higher magnification, lobulated and folded nuclear contours and immature chromatin can be appreciated (<<30707>>). Nonspecific esterase cytochemical stain highlights strongly positive monoblasts (<<30685>>).
